execution persistence and orchestration modularization has completed thirteen cuts: governed_task_adapter.py is below the 1500-line inventory threshold after extracting route-aware authority/replay validation. TaskStore focused modules reduce task_repository.py from about 12557 to 4522 lines under its existing 4600-line ceiling without a second Store, connection, clock, or transaction authority. Coordinator record validation, immutable receipts, terminal rendering, and cancellation payload helpers live in pure leaf modules. RuntimeOutbox owns the factory, publisher, publish limit, and one per-Coordinator asyncio lock; all 27 message builds bind the current command authority and all 31 drains share that instance. LocalGraphExecutionRegistry owns the process-local task map and lock, tracks the full execute_stream iteration, and cancels/joins outside its lock only after durable cancellation intent and replay binding exist. GraphCancellationRuntime owns request, continuation, exact replay, and finalization while holding only the same Store, shared RuntimeOutbox, shared LocalGraphExecutionRegistry, lease TTL, and a read-only GraphCancellationProjection; the Projection holds only the Store and builds durable terminal receipts. Neither service holds the Coordinator, a bound callback, or a new lock. Coordinator retains only the public cancellation delegate and direct execute re-entry delegation, and coordinator.py is reduced from 5860 to 4627 lines. Promotion and claim remain separate transactions, RuntimeOutbox is not a cross-process claim/CAS mechanism, production cancellation authority and controlled routing remain OFF, automatic pending-intent reconciliation/takeover/continuation is still missing, and the architecture gate remains red solely because coordinator.py is an unclassified file above 1500 lines
native_multi_node_task_graph.safe_retry_boundary: The contract path is wired, and a response lost after schedule_retry commit is exactly replayed only when Attempt, Node, Lease, Graph, Budget, BudgetUsage, and related Outboxes still match; retry budget is not charged twice. Parallel deferred children use a domain-separated node-only retry identity, keep the Graph ACTIVE, and have Coordinator response-loss integration evidence. Current Host, Scheduler, and Internal production resolvers do not emit RetryableWorkerPreparationError. Exceptions after operation reservation are never auto-retried, and CancelledError is not converted into an ordinary worker failure.
native_multi_node_task_graph.terminal_failure_boundary: Ordinary and exhausted pre-reservation resolver failures atomically close Attempt, Node, Graph, Lease and four attempt/evidence-bound Outboxes. Any existing operation reservation rejects this path, and Budget finalization remains outside the bundle.
native_multi_node_task_graph.heartbeat_boundary: After operation reservation, DurableExecutionHeartbeat renews Lease before Reservation, checkpoints worker stream events and the final result, and joins before COMMIT. Renewal response loss is exactly replayed. Any heartbeat failure yields RECOVERY_REQUIRED and forbids COMMIT, but does not provide online takeover, immediate reconciliation, or continuation.
native_multi_node_task_graph.bounded_fanout_boundary: PARTIAL_B5C_DURABLE_CANCELLATION_SHADOW / PRODUCTION_OFF. TaskGraph.completion_policy is durable and optional: legacy remains the default, while ATOMIC_GRAPH_SUCCESS_V1 requires an explicit sink result_node_id. atomic_graph_success_enabled and bounded_fanout_enabled are independent, default false, and disabled in Host, Scheduler, and Internal production composition. Application capability and grant checks run before repository admission; Coordinator direct entry requires exact all-node grants. Migration 0091 atomically commits whole-Graph success and frozen result authority. B4/0090 failure, Budget, review, and crash-re-entry semantics remain active. Migration 0092 adds verified two-phase durable cancellation, but production cancellation authority is not composed. Atomic, bounded, and cancellation production enablement is forbidden until their respective canaries pass.
native_multi_node_task_graph.cancellation_boundary: B5C shadow is implemented but production is OFF. The internal Application method requires an exact Graph-revision authority verifier and has no HTTP/UI exposure; production composition injects no verifier. Phase one durably installs an intent and fences Graph, Node, Attempt, Lease, Review/token, operation, and unauthorized effect authority before local child cancellation; publisher failure cannot suppress local cancel/join. Existing intents replay only when request_id, request_identity, source, and reason_code all match. Review create/approve/resume is fenced for the exact cancelled revision. Phase two waits for active and uncertain facts to reconcile before atomically committing Graph CANCELLED, Budget disposition, Outboxes, and a canonical decision, and terminal reads revalidate operation proof structure, digest, key, and signature. Accepted NODE effects retain delivery authority, while unauthorized NODE and incomplete-Graph GRAPH effects are fenced. 0091 success and 0092 cancellation are first-writer-wins with exact replay. Automatic cross-process reconciliation, takeover, continuation, production authority wiring, and canary remain missing.
native_multi_node_task_graph.startup_recovery_boundary: Startup is ordered migration -> task_store.recover_startup -> publisher construction -> recovery outbox publication -> later runtime activation. Recovery exceptions fail closed before route activation. ASGI derives a construction-scoped execution owner from the configured logical owner. Execute re-entry can continue a cancellation intent already bound to that Graph revision, but there is no autonomous cross-process pending-intent scanner, reconciliation worker, online takeover, or automatic continuation.
